title: Introduce token-pacing meters and deferred-span hydration for noisy endpoints
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We see persistent alert noise and high trace volume from bursty endpoints where short token microbursts (many tokens emitted in <200ms windows) trigger per-token SLO alerts and create heavy tracing load. This PR adds a lightweight token-pacing metric family and a deferred-span-hydration flow to reduce noise and trace storage while preserving investigative fidelity. What changed: 1) Telemetry: added token_pacing.{count,rate,percentile} meters at the invocation level to capture tokens/sec over short sliding windows (50ms, 200ms, 1s) plus a microburst boolean indicator. 2) Tracing: introduced deferred span hydration in the tracing pipeline: initial invocation traces are emitted as compact anchors with minimal attributes; full span bodies are stored in a short-lived side-store and only hydrated for sampled investigations, anomaly-triggered lookups, or on-demand by the console. 3) Dashboard: new dashboard token-pacing-overview with cohorted microburst heatmap, per-route pacing percentiles, and a compact hydration hit/miss chart. 4) Alerts: added an alert tuning recipe that uses paced-rate instead of raw token count for noisy routes and applies a transient-suppression backoff to reduce repeated firing for bursty traffic. 5) Docs & SDK: docs/observability/token-pacing.md and SDK helpers for clients to emit pacing hints. Rollout plan: feature gated by telemetry.feature.token_pacing; start as opt-in for Canary tenants for 48h, then progressive rollout with 10/30/100% tenant sampling over two weeks. Testing: unit tests for pacing calculators, end-to-end against the ingest pipeline with synthetic microbursts (see tests/integration/token_pacing_test.py), and load tests showing 4-10x reduction in hydrated-span write volume for bursty routes. Backwards compatibility: on by feature flag; default behavior unchanged. Related work: follow-ups expected to integrate token-pacing into adaptive batching and to extend hydration search APIs for on-demand debugging. Checklist: - [x] Telemetry collectors implemented - [x] Tracing pipeline deferred store + hydrator - [x] Dashboard panels and templates - [x] Alert recipe and runbook updates - [x] Integration + load tests - [x] Docs for operators and SDK hints

review_conversation: Maya Chen (reviewer): Nice approach, can you justify the chosen window sizes and how they interplay with batching?

Ava Martinez (author): windows chosen after load benching on bursty demo traffic; 50ms to catch microbursts, 200ms to align with typical batching thresholds, 1s for route-level pacing. Added comments in code and the doc with bench results.
Dmitri Karpov (reviewer): Concern about the hydrator side-store availability in Private installs — how do we fail gracefully?

Ava Martinez: hydrator side-store is optional; if unavailable we fallback to full-span write in the main pipeline and emit a telemetry tag (hydration_fallback=true). Added config path and migration steps to docs.
Maya Chen: CI lint flagged a styling issue in pacing_window.py; please run black/format.
Ava Martinez: fixed formatting and added unit tests for edge cases.
release_notes: Add token pacing meters (short-window percentiles and microburst indicator), deferred span hydration to reduce trace volume, new dashboard token-pacing-overview, and alert tuning recipe to suppress noisy alert churn for bursty endpoints.
